title: Federated GraphQL Gateway with Distributed Query Planning & DataLoader Batching
problem: Modern microservice architectures fracture domain data across dozens of isolated REST services, forcing client web applications to make redundant round-trips to assemble screens. Naive GraphQL gateways that resolve nested fields sequentially introduce disastrous N+1 request cascades that overwhelm downstream backends. This project builds a high-performance federated GraphQL gateway in TypeScript and Node.js. The system composes independent subgraph schemas into a unified supergraph, generates optimized distributed query execution DAGs, eliminates N+1 downstream round-trips via DataLoader request batching and entity reference resolution, and caches query plans in Redis to achieve sub-4ms routing overhead.
use_cases: Enterprise microservice unification providing single typed API entrypoint for web and mobile clients
B2B SaaS data composition joining customer accounts, billing subscriptions, and usage analytics
High-throughput developer platform exposing coherent entity graph across decentralized teams
hard_parts: Composing heterogeneous subgraph schemas into a unified federated supergraph without type conflicts
Constructing optimal distributed query execution DAGs that parallelize non-dependent downstream sub-queries
Eliminating N+1 downstream microservice request floods using DataLoader batching across entity boundaries
Managing schema versioning and live subgraph health checking with graceful partial query execution
screener_signals: Clean TypeScript codebase cleanly separating schema composition, query planners, DataLoader batchers, and execution engines
Automated N+1 stress test demonstrating that a 4-level nested query issues exactly 1 batched request per downstream service
Anti-fake verification script issuing dynamic nested entity queries and verifying downstream batch consolidation

components.name: Subgraph Schema Composition Engine
components.purpose: Merges independent subgraph schemas into a single unified supergraph with entity key directives

components.name: Distributed Query Execution Planner
components.purpose: Analyzes incoming queries and builds parallel execution directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) for downstream dispatch

components.name: DataLoader Entity Batching Service
components.purpose: Coalesces identical entity key lookups into single batched requests, eliminating downstream N+1 floods

components.name: Redis Query Plan Caching Middleware
components.purpose: Caches parsed query execution plans in Redis to bypass compilation overhead on repeated query shapes

architecture.data_flow: Client GraphQL queries arrive at the gateway; the Redis Query Plan Cache checks if a pre-compiled plan exists; on cache miss, the Distributed Query Planner constructs an execution DAG identifying dependencies between subgraphs; parallel execution steps dispatch simultaneously to downstream microservices; the DataLoader Entity Batching Service combines entity reference IDs into single batched HTTP requests; returned partial JSON payloads merge into the response shape; the final unified payload returns to client in sub-millisecond overhead.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Federated schema entity key directives guaranteeing type alignment; DataLoader per-request deduplication preventing redundant network calls.

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: a federated GraphQL gateway in TypeScript/Node.js with schema composition, query planning DAGs, and DataLoader batching.
worksheet.q2: Target users: API platform engineers, full-stack architects, and backend developers.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: microservice unification, B2B SaaS cross-service data joins, and multi-client API gateways.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 28 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 24 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 27.6 -> 28 hours. Intermediate level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: subgraph schema composition without collisions, execution DAG planning, DataLoader entity batching, and Redis plan caching.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: 4 subgraph services with 35 GraphQL types and 1,000 mock records per service. Synthetic data only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: in-memory mock subgraphs.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: Downstream subgraph latency amplification. Fallback: circuit breakers and 500ms deadlines with partial fallbacks.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: static responses. Anti-fake check 5 sends 15 dynamic entity IDs and asserts downstream inspector logs batch size of 15.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Safe; synthetic mock schemas and local services only.
